post.description:
One authentication method per connector. `sasl`: SMTP AUTH on port 587 after STARTTLS; the username (`egc-…`) and a random password are generated and returned **once** in `credentials` (only an Argon2id hash is stored; rotate it if it is lost). `source_ip`: 1–20 networks (IPv4 ≥ /16, IPv6 ≥ /48) on the port 25 relay listener; networks must be publicly routable (private, loopback, link-local, shared, documentation, multicast and reserved ranges are `400` unless the deployment sets `SMTP_CONNECTOR_ALLOW_NON_PUBLIC_NETWORKS`) and may not overlap any network of any connector (`409 Network overlaps an existing connector network`). `client_certificate`: the SHA-256 fingerprint of the client certificate presented on port 25 (globally unique, `409`), optionally restricted to networks. `requireTls` (default true) only applies to `source_ip`; the other types always need TLS. At most `SMTP_CONNECTORS_MAX_PER_ORGANIZATION` (default 50) per organization (`409`). At most 20 per caller per minute (`429`).

**Warning:** never use `source_ip` connectors for shared-IP mail platforms such as Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace: every customer of that platform sends from the same addresses and could then send as your organization. Use `sasl` or `client_certificate` connectors for them.

post.description: Fetches up to `limit` dead letters of `sourceQueue` (a work queue: `email.received`, `email.delivery.pending`; other queues are 400 `source_queue_not_replayable`) matching the optional filters, republishes each unchanged envelope to the source queue with fresh retry headers and a replay id, confirmed before the dead letter is removed. Non-matching and invalid messages stay in the queue. A replayed event that was already processed is a ledger duplicate, so replays are safe to repeat. `dryRun` changes nothing. One replay at a time platform-wide (409 `replay_in_progress`); audited as `platform.dead_letters_replayed`. 503 `dead_letter_replay_unavailable` without RABBITMQ_OPS_URL or when the broker fails (the audit row then says `partial`).
